title: The Grade Algebra
summary: Defines the grade algebra for graded monads as a preordered monoid, proves the fundamental composition theorem, and shows that the memory fragment is Presburger-decidable for affine access functions.

title: Estoque v2: Obligation Algebra and Heterogeneous Inference
summary: Formalizes the obligation algebra of a heterogeneous inference system whose GPU data plane is separated from an FPGA control plane with obligation-gated eviction and wire-speed attestation.

title: Graded Monads as Universal Compilation Target
summary: Establishes graded monads with Presburger-decidable memory grades as a compilation framework and formalizes a seven-round desugaring pipeline whose rewrites preserve semantics.

title: Three Skins, No Parser
subtitle: Token-Canonical Representation
summary: Defines a token-canonical representation in which tokens are the parse tree and three surface skins are lossless bijections over the canonical form, enabling streaming validation during generation.

title: Convergence at the Thermodynamic Limit
summary: Derives a fixed point for adversarial self-play from the thermodynamic properties of a formally verified heterogeneous inference substrate and its bandwidth envelope.

title: COUNTERFORCE
subtitle: Capability Saturation as Deterrence
summary: Applies classical deterrence theory to AI capability deployment, formalizes the game structure, and argues that mutual capability saturation is its unique stable equilibrium.

title: MARKETFORCE
subtitle: Markets as Obligation Discharge
summary: Models financial instruments as graded effects, prices as grades, and settlement as scope exit, reducing six historical governance failures to three classes of grade violation.

title: Estoque v2
subtitle: Heterogeneous Inference for Terraweight MoE Models
summary: A system design for serving terraweight mixture-of-experts models across GPU workers with a separately engineered routing and control plane.

title: Adaptive Structured Fade Distillation for Mixture-of-Experts Compression
summary: Develops a structured, budget-adaptive expert compression method with input-side rotation, per-expert fade schedules, explicit mixed-precision training, and staged distillation.

title: A Fistful of Errors
subtitle: A Discrete Formulation of Neural Network Behavior in Floating Point Representation
summary: Treats floating-point lattices as the actual object of neural computation rather than an approximation to a real-valued surface, separating constructed results, observations, and conjectures.

title: A Fistful of Errors
subtitle: The Lattice Hypothesis and a Research Program for Discrete Deep Learning
summary: States the Lattice Hypothesis as a research program and connects discrete computation to precision sensitivity, optimizer-dependent representations, quantization behavior, and inherited transformer constants.

title: Curiouser and Curiouser
subtitle: Apparent Contradictions in Neural Network Observables
summary: Frames quantization, low-rank adaptation, and sparsity as hallway-selection problems in which constraints that block wrong moves can matter more than constraints that reduce total moves.

title: Not Even Long
subtitle: An Information-Theoretic Perspective on Precision in Neural Networks
summary: Proposes that tensor precision is determined by task-relevant information content and uses Landauer's principle to distinguish reversible representation changes from destructive bit erasure.

title: The Only Thing That's Difficult Is to Forget Precisely
subtitle: The epilogue is the last reversible place to change gauges
summary: Presents a thermodynamic account of numerical precision in neural inference in which the cost of a precision transition depends on representation capacity relative to actual information content.

title: More is Less is More
subtitle: Quantized Loss Surfaces are Not Real-Valued
summary: Presents empirical evidence that discrete floating-point structure is the computational object of study, including attention collapse and recovery under aggressive quantization.

title: Not Even Long
subtitle: The Fundamental Constants of the Transformer Era Derived
summary: Argues that familiar transformer constants are hardware-conditioned evolutionary fossils and tests that account with learned scaling parameters across precision stacks.

title: Starlight is a Shadow
subtitle: The Discrete Geometry of Neural Network Optimization
summary: Studies lattice-native error metrics and precision behavior across transformer families, finding local attention collapse, coherent residual recovery, and architecture-specific bottlenecks.

title: The Polyhedral Blade
subtitle: Proof-Carrying Schedule Construction for NVIDIA-Style GPU Kernel Semantics
summary: Encodes public GPU scheduling theorems as machine-checkable propositions used to reject illegal schedules, explain unattainable correctness conditions, and emit patch-shaped diagnostics.

title: Stack Trace Relevance Filtering for Nix
subtitle: Applying Established Techniques to the MESS-B Problem
summary: Surveys program slicing, error localization, and structured diagnostics to derive a framework for minimal, causally coherent Nix error explanations that preserve semantic boundaries.

title: Reflections on Mistrusting Trust
subtitle: Closing Thompson's Loop with Cryptographic Triangulation
summary: Constructs a falsifiable build prediction checked by an independent cryptographic mechanism, including a pure Lean 4 SHA-256 implementation that reduces the remaining trust gap to collision resistance.

title: Nix Internals
subtitle: The Nuts and Bolts
summary: A technical field guide to derivations, NAR, the daemon protocol, fixed-output and content-addressed derivations, SSH transport, sandboxing, garbage collection, and substitution.

title: The Ten Laws of Intelligence
summary: Extends Asimov's three laws from robots to intelligence and grounds the resulting framework in the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, Landauer's principle, constructor theory, and mechanism design.

title: The Rewind
subtitle: On Mercy, Mechanism Design, and the Mathematics of Cooperation
summary: Studies systems in which admitting a mistake is more costly than continuing it and develops a mechanism-design account of mercy as a way to reverse that incentive.

title: The Loop
subtitle: Operating Manual for Incremental Value Delivery in the Age of Agentic Software Engineering
summary: A compact operating manual for singular KPIs, explicit delivery gates, worked examples, daily checks, and zero tolerance for process drift in agent-assisted engineering.

title: The Cassandra Problem as Bargaining Failure
subtitle: Credibility Markets, Costly Signaling, and the Political Economy of Technical Dissent
summary: A dissertation-length treatment of technical dissent as a bargaining and credibility-market problem, with costly signaling, institutional case studies, and implications for AI governance.

title: Pairwise Interlock
subtitle: Transport-Preserving Densification of Trained MoE via Fiber-Geometric Expert Annealing
summary: Develops a geometric construction for densifying a trained mixture-of-experts model by pairwise expert annealing while preserving transport structure, with a pre-anneal overlap diagnostic.

title: Proof-Carrying Autotuning
subtitle: Lean-Native Search, Costed Domain Discovery, and Certified Kernel Selection
summary: Separates broad, untrusted kernel search from compact executable certificates checked in Lean, including costed domain discovery and certified stopping over an evolving outer envelope.

title: A Man, A Plan, A Plan, A Plan
subtitle: A cost-subordinated program for the Riemann Hypothesis
summary: A theorem-ledger and certified-numerics research program for the Riemann Hypothesis based on chirality, indefinite metric, query optimality, and recovery; explicitly not a proof of RH.

title: The Dyadic Defect
subtitle: The Riemann Hypothesis as a certified-numerics problem
summary: An exposition for CUDA engineers that recasts a finite-prime reformulation of the Riemann Hypothesis as a certified-numerics instrument and research program, not a proof.

title: Finite-prime reformulations of the screw-function positivity criterion
subtitle: And a certified-numerics instrument
summary: Collects finite-prime reformulations of the screw-function positivity criterion for the Riemann Hypothesis and supplies a dual-path certified-numerics instrument, with priority ceded to M. Suzuki.

title: A State-Streaming Roofline for Kimi K3 KDA Decode on Workstation Blackwell
summary: Derives an implementation-specific recurrent-state streaming ceiling for single-token Kimi Delta Attention decode using the public TensorRT-LLM implementation, with explicit claim boundaries and validation requirements.

title: Frame Transfers in Your Reference Frame So You Can Reference While You Frame
summary: Defines frames as declared axioms plus deductions, treats messages through the deltas they induce in participant frames, and studies how those transfers compose into measurable trajectories.

title: Narsil
subtitle: Hindley-Milner Type Inference for Nix with Row Polymorphism and Cross-Language Bash Schema Extraction
summary: Presents static type inference for the dynamically typed Nix expression language, combining row-polymorphic attribute sets with schema extraction across the Nix and Bash boundary.

title: Cross-Corpus Separability Is Not Taste
subtitle: A cautionary study of embedding-space style attribution
summary: Shows that near-perfect separation between a photographer's corpus and commercial stock can be driven by corpus artifacts, then develops a camera-balanced instrument that recovers a smaller, interpretable photographic signature.
